newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro-bourses rise strongly, dollar wary.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro-bourses rise strongly, dollar wary.

text.p: European stock markets followed Wall Street ever higher on Thursday, while the dollar's rise was blocked by nagging fears of central bank intervention.
German and French shares struck yet further trading highs in a opening jump before profit-takers moved in to take the gloss off the two markets.
London also rose strongly in early trade after Wall Street leapt 1.5 percent to close at a record 6,961.63 points, tantalisingly within sight of 6,700.
Foreign exchange markets were dominated by worries that central banks could intervene to cap the dollar's surging value.

The vice-president of the German Bundesbank, Wilhelm Gaddum, told Reuters Financial TV overnight that it was not in the bank's interest to see the dollar strengthen further, echoing a similar statement from the central bank on Wednesday.
"Comments from Bundesbank officials over the last couple of days have reduced people's appetite to push dollar/mark higher for the moment," said Chris Turner, currency strategist at BZW.

By mid-morning the dollar was idling above 1.68 marks and 124 yen as the market also worried about possible Bank of Japan action against the dollar and waited for U.S. retail sales figures due at 1330 GMT.
While the Bundesbank may have dragged the dolllar down from 34-month highs it hit against the mark on Wednesday, analysts predicted the bulls would soon be baying for more blood.
European bond markets kicked off the day in a chirpy mood, with British government gilts and German bund futures sprinting to all-time highs.
"The market is holding in very well at the moment. Everything looks OK," said a gilts broker on the LIFFE futures market in London.
Wall Street's massive overnight gains, propelled by the strength of the dollar and powerful inflows into U.S. mutual funds, set the tone for another bullish day in Asian and European stock markets.
Traders predicted German shares would continue their record-setting advance after the IBIS DAX hit a record 3,243.49 points in pre-bourse trade.
"If the futures market keeps up the advance, then we could see a rally like we did on Wednesday," said one trader. German shares rose 28.56 points to 3,216.14 points in bourse trade on Wednesday.

Dealings during the bourse session could see the DAX climb to 3,250 points after the market found support from export sensitive shares, including carmakers such as Volkswagen AG, which was up 14.5 marks at 817 marks by late-morning.
But some traders said the market was overbought and was due for a correction after the recent heady gains.
French shares opened more than one percent higher and the blue-chip CAC-40 index set a fresh record high at 2,631.89 before slipping nearly 10 points on profit-taking.

Generale des Eaux was 4.5 percent higher on news it had been selected as industrial partner by railroad SNCF to operate its telecommunications network. This deal strengthens Generale des Eaux' Cegetel telecoms unit ahead of full competition with France Telecom in 1998.
Europe's largest stock market, London, also rose strongly in early trade but fell short of the record-breaking performance of its main rivals.
The market showed little reaction to British inflation data for January, which came in a little above forecasts, but the FTSE 100 index slipped off its highs.

The Bank of England has been calling for an interest rate rise but Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has resisted the pressure and analysts do not expect a rate-hike in the runup to elections due before the end of May.

Pearson Plc was at the centre of attention in early trade after the media group said it had uncovered improper accounting at its Penguin USA books unit and may have to make a charge of up to 100 million pounds ($163 million) against 1996 profits. Its shares fell eight pence to 755.5.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6837 marks and 124.24 yen compared with 1.6820 marks and 123.81 yen in late European trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 22.7 points, or 0.53 percent, at 4,327.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 22.15 points, or 0.85 percent, at 2,621.48.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 5.40 points, or 0.17 percent, at 3,221.54.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was firmer at $343.75 in early European trade compared with $341.15 at the London close. Silver was up sharply at $5.145 versus $4.90.
